To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the empirical measures of near intermediate coloured random graphs satisfy a joint large deviation principle, which in turn implies large deviation principles for a number of interesting graph parameters.

(a) the joint large deviation principles for empirical pair measure and for the empirical locality measure hold for near intermediate coloured random graph models on n vertices, (b) the large deviation principles for number of edges per vertices, the degree distribution, and the proportion of isolates hold for near intermediate random geometric graphs.

the near intermediate coloured and uncoloured random geometric graphs exhibit a phase transition at the critical density 2d/(d+1) in the sense that the large deviation principle holds for the number of isolated vertices for both models, while the large deviation principle for degree distribution and the number of edges hold for the coloured and uncolored model only in the near-intermediate regime.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the large deviation principles of the random geometric graphs.
the large deviation properties of random geometric graphs and their coloured versions.
the study of the asymptotic behaviour of the near intermediate random graph models, in the limit when the number of vertices tends to infinity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the near intermediate random graphs exhibit a transition from a sub-critical regime to a super-critical regime as a function of a certain parameter.
the large deviation principle holds true for a wide class of the near intermediate random graph models.
the near intermediate coloured models are the best candidates to model the real world networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the empirical measures of near intermediate random geometric graphs converge in distribution to a non-trivial limit.
we have obtained large deviation principles for all the above mentioned models.
we prove the joint large deviation principle in a general framework for the empirical measures and the empirical pair measure of the random geometric graphs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the near intermediate coloured models, the empirical locality measure and the empirical pair measure are exponentially equivalent, and thus the large deviation principle for empirical locality measure implies the large deviation principle with the rate function being the relative entropy for the empirical pair measures.
the large deviation principles for these quantities are the same as the large deviation principles in the Erdös-Renyi random graph model with the same average degree.

the joint large deviation principle can be proved for a wide class of random graph models, including the coloured random geometric graph, using only the large deviation principle of the empirical measure.
